svg.aria-label: The 32 x 32 tile, its four faces, the data formats, and tile order inside a matrix
svg.title: The 32 x 32 tile, its four faces, the data formats, and tile order inside a matrix
svg.text: Tiles: the unit of everything on device
full tile: 32 x 32 elements = 4 faces of 16 x 16,
stored face by face (f0, f1, f2, f3), each row-major;
half tile: 16 x 32 = faces 0 and 1 only. Stock decode
uses it for Q, the scores, the mask and the statistics
when there are <= 16 query heads; the Palu op forces
full tiles everywhere (one of the untried levers).
stock K and V caches, Palu latent caches
Phase-2 query state and rotation step
bfp8: 16 elements share one exponent, so a tile is 1024 mantissa bytes + 64 exponent bytes.
The FPU multiplies at 5 x 7 mantissa bits per pass; HiFi2 runs two passes, HiFi4 four (this study: HiFi2).
A K chunk of 512 positions x 128 dims is 16 row tiles x 4 column tiles
row-major tile order: index = i * 4 + j
column-major tile order: index = j * 16 + i
(the K chunk's layout in L1 for Q K^T, and
the order the Palu kernel packs K_rot in)
row tile i = positions 32i .. 32i+31; column tile j = head dims 32j .. 32j+31
Fig. A2. Tiles are 32 x 32; a tensor is padded to whole tiles and addressed by tile index, so every shape in the kernels is written in tiles (St, DHt, Sk_chunk_t, ...).
